load_basis: Total power capacity of the five operating Red Oak buildings that secure Compass's Oct 2025 refinancing, as reported from a Morningstar DBRS report; may not include any earlier small building
notes: Our guess (United Electric Coop) is not supported. ConnectCRE and CommercialSearch (both 2025-10-29, reporting a Morningstar DBRS report on the Red Oak refinancing) state: 'Oncor provides electricity via two on-campus substations.' Oncor is the delivery utility in the ERCOT competitive market; the retail energy seller and contract terms were not found, so arrangement is left unknown. Confidence medium because the statement is campus-level trade press and the match between the permit address (300 Houston School Rd, Compass Datacenters DFW III LLC) and the Red Oak campus rests on operator and city, not a document naming the address. Year left null because sources conflict: Compass's 2020-01-29 release said the first building, a 6 MW facility, was 'scheduled for delivery in Q2 2020' (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/compass-datacenters-adds-second-dallas-area-campus-300994816.html) and our first generator permit is 2020, but ConnectCRE says 'The five existing facilities came online between 2024 and 2025.' No source confirming actual first commercial operation was found. Load: 180 MW for five buildings, 360 MW and 10 buildings at full build-out (same articles); the 2020 release said 350+ MW of IT load. Our 706 MW is not supported by any source found. County from general knowledge of Red Oak, not from a fetched record. Lat/lon not re-verified.

site_name: Google Henderson data center, W Warm Springs Rd
notes: Utility confirmed. IREI (2020-01-21) quotes Google: it 'has submitted the necessary paperwork to secure approvals for our Long-Term Energy Supply Agreement for electric service to Google's facility in Henderson, Nevada', filed with Nevada Power Company at the Public Utilities Commission of Nevada. PV Tech (2020-01-09) reports the filing came from 'Nevada Power Co, a subsidiary of NV Energy', submitted in December 2019, paired with a 350 MW solar plus up to 280 MW storage project (generation figures, not site load). The commission's final order was not retrieved, so special_contract rests on the filing, not the approval. Year: PV Tech says the Henderson facility was 'scheduled to start operations in mid-2020'; Google's site page (https://datacenters.google/locations/henderson-nevada/) lists a 2019 groundbreaking and says the Henderson data center was 'built in 2019'. 2020 is a scheduled date, not a confirmed opening, hence low confidence. Either way our 2025 estimate (from a 2024 generator permit) is too late; the 2024 permit is more likely an expansion. No sourced load figure found; our 241 MW is unverified. County from general knowledge. Lat/lon not re-verified.

site_name: Microsoft Goodyear datacenter campus, W Broadway Rd (Azure West US 3)
notes: Our guess (Salt River Project) is wrong; the site is served by APS. Three sources: (1) APS's Cyclone-Wildcat 230kV siting page describes two customer-driven high-tech/data center projects 'northwest of the Broadway Road and Litchfield Road intersection in Goodyear' tied into the 230kV line 'south of Broadway Road between Litchfield Road and Bullard Ave' (ACC docket L-00000D-19-0196-00183, CEC Case 183, approved 2019-11-07, estimated completion 2020). The customers are not named, but the location matches 14250 W Broadway Rd. (2) Area Development (2019-08-01) on Microsoft's Goodyear and El Mirage datacenters quotes the Arizona Commerce Authority thanking 'our partners at APS for helping bring this project to life' (https://www.areadevelopment.com/newsItems/8-1-2019/microsoft-data-centes-el-mirage-goodyear-arizona.shtml). (3) SWCA's siting case study says APS 'announced the need for a new double circuit 230kV power line to serve the Microsoft data center' with 'the APS Runway Substation, located on the Microsoft site in Goodyear' (https://www.swca.com/projects/runway-substation-230kv-line-siting-project/); that may be Microsoft's second Goodyear campus rather than this address. Tariff vs special contract not found. Year: Microsoft launched the West US 3 region on 2021-06-15; the post names Goodyear and El Mirage but does not say which campus went live first, so medium. No sourced load figure; our 191.7 MW is unverified. County from general knowledge. Lat/lon not re-verified.

site_name: Amazon (AWS) New Albany campus, Smith's Mill Rd (CMH050)
notes: No document naming the utility for this specific site was found. Evidence for AEP Ohio is contextual: News 5 Cleveland reports that in the New Albany business park 'American Electric Power has built electrical substations throughout the park' and 'made major investments in the park — bringing redundant power and heavy transmission lines'; the article does not tie AEP to Amazon's Smith's Mill Rd site and does not rule out the co-op. AEP Ohio's own OPSB notices found (Badger Station, Case 23-0290-EL-BLN, at Beech Rd NW and Jug St; Kiber; Jorden) serve unnamed customers at other locations and could not be matched to this address. Licking Rural Electric was neither confirmed nor excluded. Year: not found. AWS announced on 2025-08-07 the opening of two New Albany datacenters, but those are on the Beech/Miller Road campus (https://columbusconstruction.org/3460-2/), not shown to be this site. Our 2025 estimate rests only on the 2024 generator permit. No sourced load figure; our 147.2 MW is unverified. County from general knowledge of the Johnstown/New Albany 43031 area. Lat/lon not re-verified.

site_name: Meta Fort Worth Data Center, AllianceTexas
notes: No source naming the delivery utility for this campus was found; two targeted searches came up empty. Oncor is an inference, not a finding: Site Selection (Sept 2015) quotes Facebook on choosing Fort Worth, 'In Texas, given that the market is open, we can choose the source and figure out who we want to supply energy to us', which describes retail choice. Of the utilities whose mapped territory covers the point, only Oncor is in the ERCOT competitive retail market as far as I know; the three co-ops (Tri-County, CoServ/Denton County, United) are not. I am uncertain about this and it should be confirmed against a PUC or Oncor record. Facebook's power supply was a long-term agreement with Citigroup Energy for output of a roughly 200 MW Clay County wind farm (https://www.greensourcetexas.org/articles/energy-efficient-facebook-data-center-fort-worth-be-powered-wind-farm); that is the energy seller, not the wires utility, and 200 MW is the wind farm, not site load. Year: a Tarrant County College magazine article states 'Meta's Fort Worth Data Center began operations in 2017 at AllianceTexas'; trade press found in search also reports a spring 2017 opening. Matches our 2017. No sourced load figure; our 134.4 MW is unverified. County per the same article ('north Tarrant County'). Lat/lon not re-verified.

site_name: Microsoft Project Ginger West datacenter campus, Booneville Rd
notes: Utility not established from an acceptable source, so left null. Our guess (MidAmerican Energy) was neither confirmed nor contradicted; the only mention found is generic (a Greater Des Moines Partnership data center flyer naming MidAmerican and Alliant as regional utilities, https://www.dsmpartnership.com/filesimages/2026/PDF/Data%20Centers%20Industry%20Flyer%202026.pdf), with nothing tying either to this site. Year not established: Microsoft's community page for the Ginger West project says only 'Construction is estimated to be completed by summer 2028' and that completion does not indicate operation (https://local.microsoft.com/blog/ginger-west-datacenter-construction-update/); trade press found in search reports planning approval for the first two buildings in 2021, but that article could not be fetched (403). No statement of first commercial operation was found, so our 2024 estimate rests only on the 2023 generator permit. No sourced load figure; our 104.5 MW is unverified. County left null: West Des Moines spans several counties and no fetched source states it (the coordinates suggest Dallas County). Lat/lon not re-verified.

site_name: CyrusOne DFW1 Carrollton, 1649 W Frankford Rd
load_basis: Total IT Capacity listed on CyrusOne's own DFW1 Carrollton facility page (current page, undated)
notes: Utility not established from an acceptable source, so left null. Our guess (Denton County Electric Coop / CoServ) was not confirmed. A data-center directory lists Oncor as the power provider, which is a lead only and was not used; CyrusOne's facility page does not name the utility. Year: Data Center Knowledge (2013-09-13) quotes CyrusOne's CEO: 'Our Carrollton data center, which opened in August 2012'. Our 2020 estimate is eight years late; the 2019 generator permit reflects a later expansion. Load: CyrusOne's page gives 45 MW total IT capacity and 600,000 sq ft of technical space. Older planning figures were higher and are not used: 'up to 60 megawatts of critical IT load' (same 2013 article) and 'up to 80 megawatts of power' at full build-out (https://www.datacenterknowledge.com/operations-and-management/cyrusone-adds-data-halls-in-dallas-and-houston, 2014). Our 85.2 MW is above the operator's stated IT capacity, which is plausible for total facility load but unverified. County left null: Carrollton spans Dallas, Denton and Collin counties and no fetched source states it. Lat/lon not re-verified.

load_basis: Critical IT load stated on DataBank's own LGA3 facility page
notes: Utility not named in any source fetched, so left null. Our guess (Orange & Rockland) is the only mapped candidate and was not contradicted. Westfair (2022-11-19) says the property 'includes a utility-owned substation capable of providing up to 45 megawatts of electric power' without naming the utility (https://westfaironline.com/?p=155852); DataBank's pages and the 2024 dedication coverage also do not name it. Year: at the May 2024 dedication LGA3 was 'currently under construction and will open in early 2025' (Lightwave, 2024-05-14); DataBank's page now describes it in the present tense as providing 20 MW, and a July 2026 NY DEC notice refers to 'the existing Databank Phase 1 project, which includes a 145,000 sf data center' (https://dec.ny.gov/news/environmental-notice-bulletin/2026-07-22/seqr/town-of-orangetown-databank-phase-ii). The opening announcement itself was not fetched, hence medium. Our 2024 estimate is one year early. Load: 20 MW critical IT load per DataBank; DataBank's page says 'When complete, the project will have 200,000 square feet of raised floor and 40MW of power', while 2024 coverage said 30 MW of critical power expandable to 45 MW from the on-site substation, with a possible second building (LGA4) and second 45 MW substation. Our 82.9 MW is well above any published figure. County from a search result, not a fetched record. Lat/lon not re-verified.

site_name: Google Leesburg data center, Stonewall Business Park (Hayden Technologies LLC)
notes: Utility not established, so left null. Two targeted searches found nothing naming NOVEC (our guess) or Dominion as the provider for Google's Stonewall Business Park site; Dominion transmission filings found for the Sycolin Road area do not name customers. Year: Bisnow (2024-04-29) states 'In Leesburg, Google opened its 200K SF facility on 58 acres in 2022.' This fits Google's own timeline (https://datacenters.google/locations/virginia/): 2019 'Google opens our first data center in Northern Virginia' (the Arcola site, where a 2017 Bisnow report said construction would start first) and 2021 'Google announces expansion of our second data center in Loudoun County.' It conflicts with our 2019 estimate, which rests on a 2018 generator permit; the permit may have preceded operation by several years. Single trade-press source, hence medium. No sourced load figure from an acceptable source; our 77.6 MW is unverified. Lat/lon not re-verified.

site_name: Digital Realty Franklin Park campus (Digital Chicago), W Grand Ave
notes: Utility confirmed. Data Center Knowledge (2012-06-06): 'Primary electrical service for Digital Chicago will be provided by Commonwealth Edison Company.' In November 2022 ComEd and Digital Realty cut the ribbon on a new 4-acre ComEd substation 'located on Digital Realty's data center campus' in Franklin Park (https://www.tdworld.com/substations/article/21254363/comed-cuts-ribbon-on-new-substation-serving-franklin-park-data-center-campus). Tariff vs contract and the retail energy supplier were not found. Year: the 2012 article says the first phase 'is expected to be delivered and operational by mid-2013'; that is a schedule, not a confirmed opening, hence low. It is consistent with our 2013 generator permit and would put energization one year before our 2014 estimate. Planned figure is the 2012 plan for the original three-building, 22-acre campus (twenty 1.125 MW pods, 'or 32.6 megawatts of IT load', expandable to 45 MVA); the campus has since added buildings and the 2022 substation, so current capacity is likely higher and no current figure was found. Our 69.9 MW is unverified. County from general knowledge. Lat/lon not re-verified.

site_name: Vantage Data Centers VA1 campus, Vantage Data Plaza (Ashburn/Sterling)
notes: Utility not established from a page I could read, so left null. Our guess (Dominion / Virginia Electric & Power) is the only mapped candidate; a search result summarised Vantage's campus page as saying power is provided by Dominion Energy, but Vantage's campus pages returned 404 or a generic page when fetched, so this is a lead, not a verified source. Year: Technical.ly (2019-02-21) reports Vantage 'has completed phase one of its 42-acre Ashburn, Va., campus' offering 6 MW of IT capacity, with 8 MW more due by August 2019. Matches our 2019. Planned build-out of 142 MW IT is the 2019 plan from the same article; search results indicate Vantage now advertises 206 MW of critical IT load across six data centers on 52 acres, which I could not verify directly. No sourced figure for operating load in 2025; our 66.3 MW is unverified. County from general knowledge. Lat/lon not re-verified.
